comment: Radio calls by id. Nights schedule them in their JSON. A line with "if" only plays when the player has chosen a reply with that tag (this campaign); "unless" is the opposite. Each reply can add a tag and has Dispatch's answer.

lines.text: Kestrel-4, this is Dispatch, radio check. Imogen Price. You'll be hearing a lot of me. How's the station treating you?

answer.text: That's the job. Keep it fed and keep the readings coming. They're good readings. Dispatch out.

replies.text: There were tracks outside the west door this morning.

answer.text: Fox, most likely. They come in off the sea ice looking for scraps. Don't leave food out. Dispatch out.

lines.text: Kestrel-4, Dispatch. Your midnight reading came through. North mast is low again.

answer.text: Vance completed his rotation. The paperwork isn't my department. Please log the 02:00 on time.

replies.text: Should I recalibrate the north mast?

answer.text: No. Log it as read. Don't recalibrate. That comes from above me, not from me.

lines.text: Kestrel-4, Dispatch. Tonight's the north mast inspection. The tether is on the airlock wall. Clip on before you open the outer door. Every time.
And before you ask again: I don't have anything for you on Vance.

replies.text: Understood. Clip on, check the mast, come back.

answer.text: Ninety seconds out, no more. The cold out there isn't like the cold in there. Dispatch out.

replies.text: Vance went out to that mast, didn't he?

answer.text: Everyone goes out to the mast. It's on the schedule. Clip on. Dispatch out.

lines.text: Kestrel-4... Dispatch. Your line's noisy tonight. Did you see anything out at the mast?

replies.text: Footprints. Two sets, side by side.

answer.text: Your own tracks from earlier. The wind fills them in unevenly. Get some rest between readings. Dispatch out.
Good. Nothing is the right answer. Dispatch out.

lines.text: Kestrel-4, Dispatch. Storm front tomorrow night. The helicopter is booked for 06:00 the morning after. You're nearly done.

answer.text: Hollis was before my time. The file says he was good with generators and kept a tidy station. That's all I've got.

replies.text: Good. I want to go home.

answer.text: Everyone does, by night four. Keep the lights on. Dispatch out.

lines.text: Kestrel-4, Dispatch. Change of plan. The relief crew came in early and they're walking up from the pad. Unlock the west door and leave it on the latch.

replies.text: At half one? In this wind?

answer.text: Leave it on the latch, Kestrel-4. Please.

replies.text: Understood. I'll leave it on the latch.

answer.text: Thank you. Thank you, Kestrel-4. We'll see you soon.

lines.text: What call? I haven't been on this channel since nine. There's no relief crew. Nobody is walking up from anywhere.
Tell me you didn't touch the west door.

answer.text: ...Log the 04:00. Keep the lights on. Don't open that door for anyone, including me. Dispatch out.
Keep it that way. Dispatch out.

lines.text: Kestrel, this is Imogen. The storm peaks tonight. The helicopter lands at 06:00 if the wind lets it.
From now on I'll start every call with those words. Kestrel, this is Imogen. If a call doesn't, it isn't me.

answer.text: Because I finally read Vance's file. All of it. I should have read it before I sent you up there. Imogen out.
Then you know more than I did. Keep the lights on. Imogen out.

lines.text: Kestrel-4, Dispatch. The helicopter's early. It's down by the north mast and they can't see the station in this. Come out to the mast light.

answer.text: Kestrel... this is... (static) ...come out. It's warm out by the mast. It's so warm.
We'll keep the light on for you.
